validated_results.title: Alcohol consumption, finasteride, and prostate cancer risk: results from the Prostate Cancer Prevention Trial.
validated_results.reason: Original human analysis within the Prostate Cancer Prevention Trial reporting relative risks for alcohol consumption and incident (biopsy-detected) prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: Heavy alcohol consumption (>=50 g of alcohol daily) versus lower intake, high-grade prostate cancer
extraction.population: Men participating in the Prostate Cancer Prevention Trial

sample_size.excerpt: Data for this study came from the 2129 participants in the Prostate Cancer Prevention Trial (PCPT) who had cancer detected during the 7-year trial and 8791 men who were determined by biopsy to be free of cancer at the trial end.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 2129 + 8791 = 10920

cases.excerpt: Data for this study came from the 2129 participants in the Prostate Cancer Prevention Trial (PCPT) who had cancer detected during the 7-year trial and 8791 men who were determined by biopsy to be free of cancer at the trial end.

effect_size.excerpt: In combined arms, heavy alcohol consumption (> or =50 g of alcohol daily) and regular heavy drinking (> or =4 drinks daily on > or =5 days per week) were associated with increased risks of high-grade prostate cancer (RR, 2.01 [95% CI, 1.33-3.05] and 2.17 [95% CI, 1.42-3.30], respectively); less heavy drinking was not associated with risk.

confidence_interval.excerpt: In combined arms, heavy alcohol consumption (> or =50 g of alcohol daily) and regular heavy drinking (> or =4 drinks daily on > or =5 days per week) were associated with increased risks of high-grade prostate cancer (RR, 2.01 [95% CI, 1.33-3.05] and 2.17 [95% CI, 1.42-3.30], respectively); less heavy drinking was not associated with risk.

comparison.excerpt: heavy alcohol consumption (> or =50 g of alcohol daily) and regular heavy drinking (> or =4 drinks daily on > or =5 days per week)

design.excerpt: Poisson regression was used to calculate relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) for associations of alcohol intake with prostate cancer risk.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: the authors examined the associations of total alcohol, type of alcoholic beverage, and drinking pattern with the risk of total, low-grade, and high-grade prostate cancer

parallel_r3_gate_reasons: important quantitative evidence remains missing or invalid: p_value

validated_results.title: Legume intake and the risk of cancer: a multisite case-control study in Uruguay.
validated_results.reason: Multisite hospital-based case-control study reporting a prostate cancer odds ratio for legume intake.

extraction.comparison_type: Highest versus lowest tertile of legume intake
extraction.population: Hospital-based cancer cases and controls at 11 cancer sites

sample_size.excerpt: To further explore the association between legume intake and cancer risk we conducted a case-control study of 11 cancer sites in Uruguay between 1996 and 2004, including 3,539 cancer cases and 2,032 hospital controls.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 3539 + 2032 = 5571

effect_size.excerpt: No significant association was observed between legume intake and cancers of the lung (OR = 1.03, 95% CI: 0.83-1.27), breast (OR = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.65-1.20), prostate (OR = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.64-1.18) or bladder (OR = 0.82, 95% CI: 0.57-1.17).

confidence_interval.excerpt: No significant association was observed between legume intake and cancers of the lung (OR = 1.03, 95% CI: 0.83-1.27), breast (OR = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.65-1.20), prostate (OR = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.64-1.18) or bladder (OR = 0.82, 95% CI: 0.57-1.17).

comparison.excerpt: The highest versus the lowest tertile of legume intake
